name: Red eye
caffeine: A full cup of filter coffee plus the whole espresso shot poured into it, so more than either alone.

house.ask: Not printed on the menus: ask at lineup whether there is an espresso machine, whether the bar will add a shot to brewed coffee, and the price.

what: A red eye is a cup of drip or batch brewed coffee with one shot of espresso poured into it; two shots make a black eye and three a dead eye. It is filter coffee first, so the brew must be fresh: a shot cannot rescue a stewed pot.
taste: Filter coffee with more weight: the shot adds body, a roastier edge and a touch more bitterness, while the brew keeps it long.

steps: Confirm the count: one shot red eye, two black eye, three dead eye.
Pour 8 to 10 oz of fresh coffee from a sealed airpot into a warmed mug.
Pull the shot and pour it in, leaving room for milk.
make.ratio: One shot to a mug of filter coffee
make.dose: 8 to 10 oz brewed coffee; one espresso shot
make.time: Coffee under an hour in the airpot; shot 25 to 30 seconds

serve: In a warmed mug with room at the top, milk and sugar offered as for any filter coffee. The brew comes from a sealed airpot inside its window, never a hotplate, and the shot goes in last.
story: Sources differ on the name: some tie it to the jolt, others to the sleepless, red-eyed drinker who orders it. Its siblings simply count the shots, two for a black eye, three for a dead eye.
guest: A red eye is brewed coffee with a shot of espresso added, fuller and roastier than the cup alone. Let me check the bar can add one.
watch: Black eye is two shots, dead eye three; confirm the count before you ring it in.
A shot does not fix a stale pot: coffee held on a hotplate stays flat and drying.
If the bar pulls no espresso, offer the single origin or our chicory coffee instead.

recall.prompt: How is a red eye made, and what goes in it?
recall.answer: A warmed mug of 8 to 10 oz of fresh brewed coffee with one espresso shot poured in: filter coffee with more body and a roasty edge.

quiz.q: A guest orders a black eye. How many espresso shots go into the coffee?
quiz.explain: A red eye takes one shot, a black eye two and a dead eye three.

quiz.q: Why should the coffee under the shot come from a sealed airpot?
quiz.explain: Hot is not fresh: a hotplate drives off aroma and turns acids harsher, and a shot cannot rescue that.

quiz.q: What ratio should the batch brew under a red eye follow?
quiz.explain: Batch brew runs about 55 to 65 g per litre, roughly 1:15 to 1:18; 1:2 is espresso.
